context: The traversals are preorder = [3, 9, 2, 1, 7] and inorder = [9, 3, 1, 2, 7]. All node values are distinct.
description: Preorder visits the root first, so the first element, 3, is the root.
Locate 3 in inorder. Only [9] lies to its left, and [1, 2, 7] lies to its right. The left and right subtrees therefore have one and three nodes, respectively.

Split preorder accordingly. The one element [9] after root 3 belongs to the left subtree. The remaining [2, 1, 7] belongs to the right. The two traversals of the right subtree contain the same nodes in different orders.
The left side shows the complete five-node tree for reference. The first table lists the traversal sequences for the resulting subproblems, and the second lists every connection in the tree.

frames.explanation: This splits the original problem into two independent recursive subproblems, one for each subtree.
frames.title: Splitting inorder at the root, then splitting preorder

summary: The first preorder value, 3, identifies the root. Inorder gives the left subtree [9] and the right subtree [1, 2, 7]. Their sizes then determine where to split preorder.
